Shri. Rajiv Gauba Calls for Deregulation as the Defining Feature of India's Next-Generation Reforms at Global Fintech Fest 2026
articles.full_content:
Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog, participated in a fireside chat on "From Regulation to Transformation: Building India's Next-Generation Reform Architecture" at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, a conversation spanning India's regulatory journey, the need for balance between innovation and oversight in fintech, and the institutional changes needed to sustain growth to achieve the Viksit Bharat vision.
Reflecting on the reforms of the past decade, Shri Gauba noted that measures such as the Goods and Services Tax, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, and a liberalized foreign investment regime had reshaped the economy and opened up sectors once considered off-limits to private enterprise, including defence, space and now nuclear energy.
He said the next-generation reform architecture should be defined by “deregulation”, with the focus on “nuts-and-bolts” reform, on doing away with the license – approval –permission and frequent renewals regime that prevails in different avatars. He emphasised the need to systematically review laws, regulations and administrative processes. This work, he said, is being carried out by a High-Level Committee, guided by the philosophy of Trust Based Governance espoused by the Prime Minister.
Many important reforms, he noted, fall in the domain of States and municipal governments and pointed to the work being done by the Deregulation Task Force, carrying the Trust-Based Governance principles down to the State and city level. Citing the scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment and the Urban Challenge Fund, he characterized the Center Governments approach as "cooperative federalism with a competitive edge", where scheme incentives are linked to reform milestones and projects are selected through challenge mode.
On fintech, Shri Gauba highlighted India’s phenomenal growth in the sector and how it has contributed to financial inclusion and access. He cited India's digital public infrastructure - from Aadhaar and UPI to DigiLocker and the account aggregator framework – as a model that the world can replicate, where Governments lays open, secure and interoperable rails on which private enterprise builds and innovates. He said regulation in technology-driven sectors should strike a dynamic balance between protecting public interest and allowing innovation to flourish. Regulatory frameworks, he added, should be principles-based, technology-neutral and proportionate to risk, while promoting competition, ensuring non-discriminatory access to underlying infrastructure and improving information symmetry. He also emphasised the need for greater coordination among financial regulators, simpler and more predictable compliance processes, and continued efforts to reduce frictions and interoperability gaps.

First-ever district-level estimates released by NSO for unincorporated non-agricultural sector
articles.full_content:
Top 50 districts drive nearly one-third of the sector’s activity Women comprise one-third of workforce in 237 districts
• NSO disseminates district-level estimates from a large-scale, nation-wide enterprise survey for the first time, marking a significant step towards strengthening granular sub-state-level statistics in India.
• The top 50 districts, ranked by the number of unincorporated establishments, account for nearly one-third of the total establishments, workforce and Gross Value Added.
• Roughly one-third of all districts have more than one lakh unincorporated establishments per district.
• In 237 districts, women constitute one-third of the total workforce in the unincorporated sector.
• In 280 districts, GVA per worker exceeds the all-India average indicating relatively higher levels of economic productivity in these districts.
NSO Releases insights on urban unincorporated enterprise landscape at district level
The importance of granular and high-frequency data has grown significantly in recent years, reflecting the increasing need for evidence-based policymaking and targeted interventions. In particular, sub-state-level statistics play a crucial role in identifying regional variations, emerging strengths and areas requiring attention, thereby enabling more targeted and area-specific policy interventions.
As part of this endeavour, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has already published, for the first time, a comprehensive statistical profile of the unincorporated sector across the country’s 46 million-plus cities, identified on the basis of Census 2011 population. Taking this initiative further, MoSPI has now presented a district-level portrait of the scale, structure and economic performance of India’s unincorporated non-agricultural sector across States and Union Territories (UTs). The district-level estimates presented in this report also include the corresponding estimates for million-plus cities located within the respective districts. This marks the first initiative of the National Statistics Office (NSO), MoSPI, to disseminate district-level estimates from a large-scale, nationwide survey. The report is available on the website of the Ministry at https://mospi.gov.in .
Unincorporated Sector at the District Level: Insights from ASUSE 2025
Drawing upon ASUSE 2025 data, this report presents a comprehensive picture of the unincorporated sector at the district level through a balanced set of indicators covering the scale and structure of establishments, employment and emoluments, and economic performance. These include estimates of establishments and workers, ownership and employment structure, women’s participation, registration status, emoluments per hired worker, and GVA per establishment and GVA per worker for market establishments. Small Hydro Power has a distinctive role in India’s clean energy transition: Shri Shripad Yesso Naik
articles.full_content:
India’s assessed Small Hydro Power potential stands at around 21 GW across more than 7,100 identified sites Small Hydro Power Session to Feature at Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026; Curtain Raiser Organised
Small Hydro Power has a distinctive role in India’s clean energy transition, said Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for New and Renewable Energy and Power while addressing the Curtain Raiser Programme for the dedicated Small Hydro Power (SHP) session at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 held today in New Delhi. Addressing the gathering, he said that Small Hydro Power can contribute to energy security, decentralised generation, employment and socio-economic development in remote areas.
Shri Naik said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India’s clean energy journey has undergone a remarkable transformation, propelling the country to the forefront of the global energy transition. He said renewable energy has emerged as a powerful instrument of energy security, economic growth, technological progress and employment generation.
The Minister highlighted that India has crossed the milestone of 300 GW of installed non-fossil-fuel capacity. He said the strength of India’s energy transition lies in building a diverse, balanced and resilient energy portfolio suited to the country’s geography, resources and development needs.
Shri Naik emphasised the significant potential of Small Hydro Power in this context. He said India’s presently assessed Small Hydro Power potential is around 21 GW across more than 7,100 identified sites, of which only about 5.2 GW has been harnessed. He noted that this represents a significant opportunity for further development of the sector.
Shri Naik said the significance of Small Hydro Power goes beyond adding generating capacity. He noted that, wherever technically and environmentally feasible, appropriately designed run-of-river projects can provide a renewable energy option requiring relatively less land and avoiding the large-scale submergence and displacement associated with major reservoir-based projects.
He said Small Hydro Power can provide dependable renewable electricity closer to the point of consumption, strengthen decentralised generation and contribute to the resilience of the power system, particularly in geographically challenging regions. The sector can also create employment, support local enterprises and generate economic opportunities in remote areas while maintaining sensitivity towards ecology and local communities.
The Minister highlighted the Government’s proposed Small Hydro Power Development Scheme for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, with an outlay of ₹2,584.60 crore and a target of approximately 1,500 MW of new Small Hydro Power capacity. The Scheme will also incentivise States to prepare Detailed Project Reports for about 200 projects, thereby creating a pipeline of Small Hydro Power projects for future development.

Awareness programme on “Branding and marketing under PM Vishwakarma scheme” held at Hailakandi
articles.full_content:
A one-day awareness programme on “Branding and Marketing under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme” was organized on 7 September at Hailakandi with the objective of enhancing the branding, marketing, digital, and export capabilities of artisans and beneficiaries covered under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme. The programme was organized by the Branch MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Silchar, in cooperation with the District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC), Hailakandi, and Keshav Smarak Sanskrit Surbhi.
The programme was inaugurated by Shri Jay Vikas, IAS, District Commissioner, Hailakandi. In his inaugural address, Shri Vikas appreciated the initiatives undertaken by the Ministry of MSME under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme for the welfare and development of traditional artisans. He urged the beneficiaries to participate in the sessions with attention and dedication and learn effective ways of marketing, selling and exporting their products. He encouraged the artisans to focus on quality and effective marketing so that traditional products of Hailakandi gain wider recognition and establish the identity of the district in the region.
Shri G. C. Das, Assistant Director In-Charge, Branch MSME-DFO, Silchar, explained the objectives, features and benefits of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and highlighted the opportunities available to artisans under the scheme.
Shri Nurul Amin, General Manager, DICC, Hailakandi, briefed the participants about various other government schemes and initiatives that PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries can avail of for further development and expansion of their enterprises.
Shri S. G. Gundayya, Assistant Director Grade-I, Branch MSME-DFO, Silchar, highlighted the performance and progress of Hailakandi district under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and emphasized the importance of coordinated efforts among implementing agencies and beneficiaries.
The technical sessions covered key aspects of entrepreneurship, pricing, market trends, financial and digital management, exports, packaging and product quality. As part of the digital facilitation initiatives, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) assisted artisans in generating QR codes for digital transactions. The participants were also facilitated with onboarding on various e-commerce platforms to enable them to access wider online markets.
The programme provided PM Vishwakarma artisans with practical knowledge on branding, marketing, digital payments, e-commerce, packaging, quality and exports, supporting their efforts to expand their market reach and develop sustainable, market-oriented enterprises.
articles.summary: A one-day awareness programme on “Branding and Marketing under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme” was organized on 7 September at Hailakandi with the objective of enhancing the branding, marketing, digital, and export capabilities of artisans and beneficiaries covered under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme. The programme was organized by the Branch MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Silchar, in cooperation with the District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC), Hailakandi, and Keshav Smarak Sanskrit Surbhi. The programme was inaugurated by Shri Jay Vikas, IAS, District Commissioner, Hailakandi.

PM Vishwakarma Awareness Workshop on Branding and Marketing Held in Mon
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, through the MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Dimapur, in collaboration with the Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Nagaland, and the District Industries Centre (DIC), Mon, successfully organized a one-day Awareness Workshop on Branding and Marketing under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme at the Town Council Hall, Mon, on 09 September 2026.
The workshop was designed to strengthen the entrepreneurial and business capabilities of PM Vishwakarma artisans by equipping them with practical knowledge on product packaging, labelling and design, business development, export opportunities, Artificial Intelligence (AI), e-commerce, QR code generation, and financial literacy. A total of 126 stage-3 verified artisans , including carpenters, masons, basket makers and barbers from different parts of Mon district, participated enthusiastically in the workshop.
The event commenced with a welcome address by Shri M. Chingo, Functional Manager, DIC Mon , who welcomed the participants and highlighted the importance of enhancing market access and business skills among artisans. This was followed by the keynote address delivered by Shri Shekhozo Vero, EAC Mon , who emphasized the significance of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme in empowering traditional artisans and strengthening their livelihoods.
In his address, Shri Vero underscored the commitment of the Ministry of MSME and the Government of Nagaland towards supporting genuine artisans through marketing assistance, skill upgradation, credit linkages, and various enterprise development initiatives. Encouraging artisans to adopt an entrepreneurial mindset, he remarked that while an artisan generally produces based on customer orders, an entrepreneur focuses on production and market creation regardless of existing demand. He stressed that artisans of Mon district possess immense potential due to the uniqueness, quality, and craftsmanship reflected in their products.
Speaking about the growing demand for handmade products, Shri Vero noted that handmade goods continue to command strong market value globally due to increasing consumer preference for authentic and handcrafted items, despite a limited number of producers. Expressing optimism about the future of local products, he stated, “I believe we will be able to find Mon artisanal products across the country in the coming years as well as in international markets.”
The first technical session on Product Packaging, Labelling and Design was delivered by Smt. Allen Konyak, Founder, Ipseity Bake & Co., Mon . The session focused on the importance of developing products based on customer needs and market demand. articles.title: PM Vishwakarma Awareness Programme Organised at Thadlaskein, West Jaintia Hills
articles.full_content:
The Branch MSME Development & Facilitation Office (BrMSME DFO), Shillong, Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India, organised a PM Vishwakarma Awareness Programme at Thadlaskein C&RD Block, West Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya, on 10 September 2026. The programme focused on branding and marketing of products made by PM Vishwakarma artisans.
Sh. Prabhat Kumar Singh, IEDS, Assistant Director Grade-I, BrMSME DFO, Shillong, made a presentation on the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and its various components. The programme included sessions on branding and marketing, product packaging, use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), financial literacy, digital payments and QR-code generation, social security schemes and Udyam Registration.
The programme followed a multi-departmental convergence approach, with participation from officials and representatives of the Directorate of Commerce & Industries, Government of Meghalaya, State Bank of India, India Post Payments Bank and other stakeholders. Information on relevant Government schemes, financial services and support available to artisans was shared during the sessions.
An Udyam Registration facilitation camp was also organised for artisans. The programme included sharing of artisan success stories to provide participants with practical insights into enterprise development, market access and utilisation of Government support.
The programme was organised with the objective of creating awareness among traditional artisans regarding available institutional support and opportunities for skill development, formalisation, finance, digital adoption, branding and market access under PM Vishwakarma and other relevant Government initiatives.
articles.summary: The Branch MSME Development & Facilitation Office (BrMSME DFO), Shillong, Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India, organised a PM Vishwakarma Awareness Programme at Thadlaskein C&RD Block, West Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya, on 10 September 2026. The programme focused on branding and marketing of products made by PM Vishwakarma artisans. Prabhat Kumar Singh, IEDS, Assistant Director Grade-I, BrMSME DFO, Shillong, made a presentation on the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and its various components.

MNRE Hosts BRE Summit 2026 Roadshow in Lucknow, Highlights Opportunities Across North India’s Renewable Energy Landscape
articles.full_content:
MNRE Takes BRE Summit 2026 Roadshow to Lucknow, Building Regional Momentum for India's Largest Renewable Energy Summit & Expo Roadshow brings together government representatives and clean energy stakeholders from Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Bihar ahead of the November summit in New Delhi
Lucknow, September 10, 2026: Building on the momentum generated across five regional editions in Jaipur, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Bengaluru, leading voices from government, industry and the renewable energy sector gathered today in Lucknow for the sixth in a series of regional roadshows for the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRE Summit) 2026, India's largest renewable energy summit and expo. The Lucknow edition brought a distinct regional dimension to the outreach series, convening representatives from Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Bihar in a single forum and placing North India's growing stake in the country's clean energy transition firmly at the centre of the conversation. The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 will be held alongside the 9th Session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH), from 2-5 November 2026, bringing together global leaders, policymakers, industry, investors and innovators on a common platform. The Lucknow roadshow, hosted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), opened with introductory remarks by Shri Ramakrishna Satluri, CEO, Shakti Pumps and National Governing Council Member, NSEFI. Shri AK Sharma, Hon'ble Minister of Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, who was the Chief Guest for the event, in his address said “Uttar Pradesh is committed to playing a leading role in India’s clean energy transition by accelerating renewable energy deployment and creating a conducive ecosystem for investment, innovation and industry participation. The BRE Summit 2026 offers an important national and global platform for Uttar Pradesh to showcase its growing clean energy opportunities, connect with investors and technology partners, and strengthen collaboration across the renewable energy value chain. I invite industry, investors and clean energy stakeholders from across India and the world to participate in the Summit and partner with Uttar Pradesh in building a cleaner and more sustainable energy future”. He further appreciated the overwhelming participation witnessed at the Lucknow Roadshow, reflecting the scale at which the event was organized in the capital city. In his address, Dr. Ashish Kumar Goel, IAS, Additional Chief Secretary, Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, said “Uttar Pradesh is rapidly emerging as a significant force in India’s renewable energy landscape, supported by a progressive policy framework spanning solar, bioenergy, green hydrogen and electric mobility. With robust transmission infrastructure, ongoing expansion of the Green Energy Corridor and planned capacity to facilitate large-scale renewable and pumped storage

articles.full_content:
Berhampore, Murshidabad, September 9, 2026
Press Information Bureau (PIB), Kolkata, organised a media workshop 'Vartalap' in Berhampore, Murshidabad, today, aiming at strengthening engagement with grassroots level journalists and facilitating effective dissemination of information on government initiatives and development programmes. The programme focused on key issues including Ayushman Bharat, Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), child trafficking and other development initiatives of the Union Government.
Addressing the gathering, the Director General (Eastern Zone), PIB and CBC, Shri T. V. K. Reddy, emphasised the importance of PIB Vartalap in establishing a direct interface with journalists working at the grassroots level. He highlighted the role of journalists in ensuring that authentic and verified information reaches people, particularly in rural and underserved areas. Shri Reddy also spoke about the Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 and the Press Sewa Portal, which facilitates smoother registration and processing for periodicals. He the urged journalists to make effective use of the PIB website as a reliable source of information for professional and development-oriented journalism.
The Minister for Mass Education Extension and Library Services and Backward Classes Welfare, Government of West Bengal, Shri Gouri Sankar Ghosh, stressed the importance of disseminating fact-based and authentic news. He highlighted the significance of major government initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and Swachh Bharat Yojana, and emphasised the need for effective implementation of government schemes so that their benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.
Speaking on healthcare initiatives, the Chief Medical Officer of Health, Murshidabad, Dr. Sandip Sanyal, underlined the importance of effective information dissemination regarding government health initiatives. He explained the process of availing benefits under Ayushman Bharat and urged journalists to create awareness among beneficiaries regarding e-KYC and facilitate informed access to the scheme through responsible dissemination of information. He also highlighted the importance of the ABHA ID and digital health records, besides discussing maternal health programmes and initiatives for the eradication of tuberculosis. The session was followed by an interactive question-and-answer session.
The Lead District Manager, Punjab National Bank, Shri Fajal Mamud, elaborated on the significance of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in promoting financial inclusion. He projected the financial inclusion achievements in the Murshidabad district of West Bengal and the role of such initiatives in ensuring greater access to formal banking services, including for women and other sections of society. Union Budget 2026-27 Accelerating Chhattisgarh's Inclusive Development and Economic Growth: Shri Ramdas Athawale
articles.full_content:
Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment reviews welfare schemes and central flagship initiatives in Raipur
Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, addressed the media during his official visit to Chhattisgarh, highlighting that the Union Budget 2026-27 is providing a strong financial impetus to the state's all-round development under the vision of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas'. The Union Minister noted that a tax devolution of ₹50,427 crore has been proposed for Chhattisgarh in the Union Budget, alongside a grant provision of ₹15,000 crore for FY 2025-26 to bolster the state's financial capability and infrastructure works. Presenting the progress of central flagship schemes in the state, Shri Athawale stated that central social security and welfare programs are creating a transformative impact on rural, poor, and tribal communities across Chhattisgarh.
Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, more than 1.88 crore bank accounts have been opened in the state, securing financial inclusion with deposits amounting to over ₹9,324 crore. Furthermore, over 39.75 lakh gas connections have been allotted in Chhattisgarh under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, providing clean cooking fuel to rural households. Highlighting infrastructure and health developments, the Minister underlined that approval for 5 new medical colleges has been granted to expand medical education and healthcare infrastructure in the state.
Additionally, an Indian Oil bottling plant constructed at a cost of over ₹130 crore in Korba is driving logistics, local employment, and energy security in the region. Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban), over 1.77 lakh houses have been constructed with an allocation of ₹4,699 crore, while under the Ujala Scheme, 1.08 crore LED bulbs have been distributed across the state.
The Union Minister re-affirmed the Central Government's focus on the welfare of marginalized communities, adding that funding has been provided for 5 De-addiction Centres and 3 Old Age Homes in the region to support social defense initiatives. Earlier in the day, Shri Athawale chaired a high-level review meeting with senior officials of the Chhattisgarh government and the Raipur Municipal Corporation to assess the implementation of social welfare programs and review the progress of SC/ST backlog recruitment.

The Union Minister noted that a tax devolution of ₹50,427 crore has been proposed for Chhattisgarh in the Union Budget, alongside a grant provision of ₹15,000 crore for FY 2025-26 to bolster the state's financial capability and infrastructure works. Presenting the progress of central flagship schemes in the state, Shri Athawale stated that central social security and welfare programs are creating a transformative impact on rural, poor, and tribal communities across Chhattisgarh.

MSDE Organises ‘Skill Manthan’ on 'Building Sustainable Livelihoods for Women'
articles.full_content:
Districts are the engines of economic growth and reform : Shri Jayant Chaudhary at the inaugural session of ‘Skill Manthan’
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised the inaugural session of ‘ Skill Manthan’ centred on the theme ‘Building Sustainable Livelihoods for Women’. The virtual dialogue highlighted innovative initiatives from Meerut and Bijnor in Uttar Pradesh and NTR District in Andhra Pradesh, demonstrating how district administrations can combine skilling, entrepreneurship, finance, technology, and market access to create sustainable livelihood opportunities for women. ‘Skill Manthan’ will serve as a knowledge-sharing platform to showcase innovative and impactful district-led initiatives.
Speaking on the initiative, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, said, “District administrations are the true engines of growth, reform and transformation. Through our district-led planning approach, we are ensuring that skilling initiatives are driven by local needs and aligned with the requirements of industry, particularly MSMEs. Supported by District Skill Development Plans, the skilling agenda is at the forefront of district administration, enabling more responsive, demand-driven and impactful outcomes for youth and local economies.”
Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said, “India’s skilling aspirations can only be realised when skill development is driven by local realities. Hyperlocal skilling, aligned to district needs and employment opportunities, is essential to equip our youth with relevant skills and connect them to meaningful livelihoods in a rapidly evolving economy.”
District Collectors and District Magistrates, Ms. Jasjit Kaur of Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, Dr. G. Lakshmisha of NTR, Andhra Pradesh and Dr. Vijay Kumar Singh of Meerut, Uttar Pradesh showcased innovative pathways for women’s economic empowerment through skilling, entrepreneurship, and market integration. Meerut demonstrated a women-centric manufacturing model that provides hands-on training and employment in badminton racket and shuttlecock production. Bijnor highlighted Vidur Prerna Swadeshi, a district-wide platform enabling rural women entrepreneurs through branding, market access, and enterprise support. NTR District’s RISE showcased a one-stop ecosystem offering skilling, credit facilitation, mentoring, employment linkages, and entrepreneurial support, illustrating how local institutions can be converged to create sustainable opportunities for women-led enterprises.
The session reaffirmed MSDE’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with district administrations and creating a national platform for documenting, sharing, and replicating successful grassroots models. Self-assembly of organic molecules opens a new path to green hydrogen production
articles.full_content:
A simple yet powerful strategy of integrating naturally occurring amino acid with a light-absorbing organic molecule could improve solar driven hydrogen production using completely metal free organic materials.
Hydrogen is considered one of the most promising clean energy carriers because its combustion produces only water, making it an environmentally benign alternative to fossil fuels. One of the promising methods for producing green hydrogen is by using sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. However, most existing photocatalysts rely on inorganic semiconductors or precious metals, which are often expensive, difficult to manufacture, and raise concerns regarding long-term sustainability. Developing efficient metal-free organic photocatalysts has therefore remained a major scientific challenge.
A team of researchers from the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, -an autonomous institute under Department of Science and Technology (DST), integrated a naturally occurring amino acid (aspartic acid) with a light-absorbing organic molecule, perylene diimide (PDI) and allowed the molecules to spontaneously organize themselves through supramolecular self-assembly.
They found that the enhanced performance arises from how the molecule organizes itself. The amino acid moiety promotes strong, extended hydrogen bonding, while the PDI chromophore drives π–π stacking and efficient light absorption.
Thus, the synergistic interplay between the two governs the molecular organization and, consequently, the functional properties of the material.
The researchers synthesised an aspartic acid-functionalized perylene diimide (PDI) molecule that spontaneously self-assembled in water into highly ordered two-dimensional nanosheets.
This subtle molecular reorganization dramatically broadened light absorption, enhanced charge separation, reduced energy losses, and increased the accessible surface area for catalytic reactions without altering the molecule's chemical composition. As a result, the self-assembled material generated nearly 18% higher photocurrent than its bulk counterpart during solar-driven water splitting.
Advanced electrochemical measurements together with density functional theory (DFT)
calculations further revealed that self-assembly promotes more efficient charge transport, while the amino acid increases the molecular dipole moment, facilitating effective separation of photo-generated charges that drive hydrogen evolution.
The study further demonstrates that naturally occurring amino acids can serve not only as molecular building blocks but also as powerful regulators of supramolecular organization and photocatalytic performance. This molecular design strategy offers a sustainable route to developing efficient, environmentally friendly, and metal-free photocatalysts for solar energy conversion.

articles.full_content:

A press conference on ‘Solid Waste Management’ was organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Dehradun, under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, at the Secretariat Media Centre on Wednesday. Detailed information was shared on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, dumpsite remediation, waste segregation, air pollution control and the role of local bodies.
Dr Parag Madhukar Dhakate, Member Secretary, Pollution Control Board, said that the quantity of waste is increasing with rapid urbanisation. In this context, it is essential to take scientific and data-driven approaches to the grassroots level and ensure the active participation of public representatives and citizens. The goals of effective solid waste management and clean air can be achieved not through government efforts alone, but through collective participation.
He said that under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, which came into effect from 1 April 2026, emphasis has been placed on segregating waste into four streams—wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste. The responsibilities of Bulk Waste Generators (BWGs) have also been strengthened, with a provision for Extended Bulk Waste Generators Responsibility (EBWGR). The Rules provide for online monitoring of waste collection, transportation, processing and disposal, along with digital registration and reporting. The objective is to enhance transparency and accountability, promote the use of waste as a resource and strengthen the circular economy. Recycling and reuse have been prioritised, while landfill has been kept as the last resort.
Dr Dhakate emphasised that 100 per cent door-to-door waste collection is being provided across 1,314 wards under 108 Urban Local Bodies in Uttarakhand. Around 1,515 vehicles are currently available, while procurement of additional vehicles is underway. New vehicles are being equipped with four compartments for four-stream segregation. Source segregation has already been initiated in 1,225 wards. Approximately 1,930.85 metric tonnes of waste is generated daily in the state, of which 1,804.59 metric tonnes (93.46 per cent) is processed every day.
